subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb form: 'Neither of the students ______ ready.'
explanation: With 'neither' the subject is singular; use a singular verb. 'Neither of the students was ready' follows subject–verb agreement for singular indefinite pronouns.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence shows correct subject–verb concord?
options: A number of teachers is attending the conference.
A number of teachers are attending the conference.
The number of teachers are impressive.
Every of the teachers were present.
explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('are attending'); contrast with 'The number of' which takes a singular verb.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect?
options: By the time she arrived, we have left.
By the time she had arrived, we left.
By the time she arrived, we had left.
By the time she arrives, we had left.
explanation: Past perfect ('had left') expresses an action completed before another past action ('she arrived'); this is the proper past perfect sequence.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'meticulous'?
explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise; 'thorough' is the closest synonym, unlike careless, hasty or sloppy.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'If you don't pull your weight, the team will suffer,' 'pull your weight' means:
options: do one’s fair share of work
explanation: The idiom 'pull your weight' means to do your fair share of the work; it does not refer to strength, belongings, or complaining.

subject: English Language
text: Which is the correctly punctuated and capitalised sentence for: 'tomorrow we meet in lagos nigeria'?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
Tomorrow we meet in Lagos, Nigeria.
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Cities and countries are proper nouns and capitalised; a comma separates city and country: 'Lagos, Nigeria.' The sentence also needs initial capital 'Tomorrow'.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: 'table', 'about', 'relax', 'include'?
explanation: 'Table' has primary stress on the first syllable ('TA-ble'); 'about' and 'include' are stressed on the second syllable, and 'relax' on the second syllable as a verb.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: beat, seat, meat, mate?
explanation: 'Beat', 'seat', 'meat' share the /iː/ vowel sound; 'mate' has a diphthong /eɪ/, so it is the different vowel sound.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main speech function of: 'Could you pass the salt?'
explanation: The modal question 'Could you pass the salt?' functions as a polite request, not an offer, apology, or simple declarative statement.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They will finish the project next month.'
options: The project will finish next month.
The project will be finished next month.
The project is finished next month by them.
The project will be being finished next month.
explanation: Future passive requires 'will be' + past participle: 'will be finished.' Option A correctly forms the passive for future tense.

subject: English Language
text: If you _____ earlier, you would have caught the bus.
explanation: Third conditional uses past perfect in the 'if' clause: 'If you had left earlier, you would have caught the bus.' 'Had left' is required.

subject: English Language
text: Tolu watered the plant every morning but kept it in a dark cupboard. The plant died. What is the most likely reason?
explanation: Given the plant was kept in a dark cupboard, lack of sunlight is the most plausible cause of death; watering alone cannot substitute for light.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb form: 'Every one of the players ____ ready.'
explanation: Use singular verb with 'every one of' + plural noun; 'every one' is singular, so 'is' is required.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: 'By the time she arrived, we ______ for two hours.'
explanation: Past perfect continuous ('had been practising') shows an action in progress that continued up to a past point.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'abridge'?
explanation: 'Abridge' means to shorten or condense a text; 'shorten' is the closest synonym among the options.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'Keep your nose to the grindstone,' what does the idiom mean?
explanation: The idiom 'keep your nose to the grindstone' means to work hard and persistently; it refers to steady effort.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised version of: 'once upon a time in abuja, there lived a tailor.'
options: Once upon a time in Abuja, there lived a tailor.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals for sentence start and proper noun 'Abuja', comma after introductory place phrase is optional but option 1 is fully correct and ends with a period.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: 'banana', 'apple', 'market', 'doctor'?
explanation: 'Banana' has primary stress on the second syllable (ba-NA-na); the others have stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: 'ship', 'sit', 'sip', 'sheep'?
explanation: 'Sheep' has the long /iː/ vowel, while 'ship', 'sit' and 'sip' have the short /ɪ/ vowel; 'sheep' differs.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main speech function of: 'I can't make it on Friday; can we meet Monday?'
explanation: The speaker cannot attend Friday and requests a different time; the primary function is to ask to reschedule.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'They will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: The results will be announced tomorrow.
explanation: Correct passive: 'The results will be announced tomorrow.' maintains future tense and places the object as subject.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the conditional: 'If only he ____ earlier, he wouldn't be in trouble now.'
explanation: Use third conditional for past regret affecting present: 'If only he had called earlier' expresses past action contrary to fact.

subject: English Language
text: Read: 'The committee deferred the decision until further notice.' What is implied?
options: The decision was finalized in private.
The decision was passed to another group.
explanation: 'Deferred until further notice' implies postponement with no set date; it does not mean rejection or delegation.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct article: 'He is ___ honourable man.'
explanation: Use 'an' before words beginning with a silent h (honourable) because the initial sound is a vowel; therefore 'an' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb form to complete: "Either the manager or the assistants ____ responsible for the error."
explanation: Use singular verb with 'Either...or' when the nearer subject (assistants) is plural normally would take plural, but grammar guides often prefer agreement with the nearer noun; here formal preference is plural 'are'. However in this construction with 'Either the manager or the assistants' the correct singular/plural depends on nearest subject: since 'assistants' is plural the correct verb is 'are'. Explanation corrects to reflect nearest-subject agreement rule.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: "By the time we arrived, the guests ____."
explanation: Use past perfect (had left) to show one past action completed before another past action; 'had left' precedes 'arrived'.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'sparse'?
explanation: 'Sparse' means thinly distributed or scanty; 'thin' matches that semantic range whereas 'lavish' is the opposite and others unrelated.

subject: English Language
text: In "He spilled the beans during the meeting," what does 'spilled the beans' mean?
explanation: The idiom 'spill the beans' means to reveal a secret or disclose confidential information; context of meeting supports 'confessed a secret'.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised version of: "on saturday, mrs ade bought a new car from aso."
options: On Saturday, Mrs Ade bought a new car from Aso.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals for sentence start and proper names (On Saturday, Mrs Ade) and capitalisation for 'Aso' as a proper noun; commas after introductory adverbial optional but first option is conventional and correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: 'around', 'market', 'memory', 'instant'?
explanation: 'Around' has primary stress on the second syllable (a-ROUND). The other words have primary stress on the first syllable (MAR-ket, MEM-o-ry, IN-stant). This tests syllable stress placement.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: 'made', 'mate', 'maim', 'mat'?
explanation: 'Made', 'mate' and 'maim' contain the /eɪ/ diphthong; 'mat' contains the short /æ/ vowel, so 'mat' differs by vowel quality.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main speech function of: "Would you mind opening the window?"
explanation: The form 'Would you mind...?' is a polite request asking someone to perform an action, not an offer, apology or complaint.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: "Someone stole the bicycle yesterday."
explanation: Past simple passive uses 'was' + past participle: 'The bicycle was stolen yesterday.' Other options are ungrammatical or incorrect tense/form.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: "If she ____ harder last year, she would have passed."
explanation: Third conditional: past unreal in the past uses past perfect in the if-clause: 'If she had studied... she would have passed.' This contrasts completed past action and hypothetical result.

subject: English Language
text: Samira left her umbrella at home. It started to rain and she waited under a shop's awning but reached home soaked. What is the most reasonable inference?
options: The awning was made of fabric and absorbed water.
She preferred getting wet to carrying an umbrella.
She had no umbrella and got wet in the rain.
The shop owner refused her shelter.
explanation: Given she left her umbrella and later arrived soaked, the reasonable inference is lack of umbrella led to getting wet; other options add unsupported assumptions beyond text.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb: "Five kilometres ____ a long walk for him."
explanation: Measurements used as a single distance are treated as singular subjects: 'Five kilometres is a long walk.' Rule: units of measurement as a whole take singular verb.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the chairman nor the members _____ aware of the amended schedule.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the nearer subject 'members' (plural), so use 'are'. This is subject–verb proximity rule.

subject: English Language
text: By 8 p.m. the students ______ their project for four hours.
explanation: Duration before a past reference uses past perfect continuous: 'had been working on' shows an action in progress up to a past time.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'perfunctory'?
explanation: 'Perfunctory' means done with minimal effort or attention; 'cursory' matches this, unlike 'careful' or 'detailed'.

subject: English Language
text: In politics, to 'throw one's hat into the ring' most nearly means:
explanation: The idiom means to enter a contest or declare candidacy; it does not mean to criticise, withdraw, or celebrate.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly capitalised sentence: 'on monday, chief adeoye visited the university of ibadan.'
options: On Monday, Chief Adeoye visited the University of Ibadan.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Proper nouns, titles and days are capitalised: 'On Monday, Chief Adeoye visited the University of Ibadan.' is fully correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: 'majority', 'teacher', 'market', 'library'?
explanation: 'majority' is stressed ma-JOR-i-ty (second syllable). 'teacher', 'market', 'library' have primary stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel quality from the others: 'cat', 'cap', 'cart', 'cab'?
explanation: 'cart' contains a long /ɑː/ or r-coloured vowel, while 'cat', 'cap', 'cab' use the short /æ/ vowel; thus 'cart' differs.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main speech function of: 'Don't forget to switch off the generator before you leave.'?
explanation: This sentence reminds someone to perform an action; it functions as a reminder rather than a warning, apology or permission-seeking.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They will hold the conference in Lagos next year.'
options: The conference will be held in Lagos next year.
The conference will hold in Lagos next year.
Lagos will be held the conference next year.
The conference held will be in Lagos next year.
explanation: Active 'They will hold the conference' correctly becomes passive: 'The conference will be held in Lagos next year.' Other forms are ungrammatical.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: 'If I _____ you, I would accept the offer.'
explanation: Present unreal conditional uses subjunctive 'were' for all persons: 'If I were you...' is the grammatically correct choice.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct reported speech form of: 'Musa said, "I will submit the essay tomorrow."'
options: Musa said he will submit the essay tomorrow.
Musa said he has submitted the essay tomorrow.
Musa said he would submit the essay the next day.
Musa said he is going to submit the essay yesterday.
explanation: Backshift in reported speech changes 'will' to 'would' and 'tomorrow' to 'the next day': 'Musa said he would submit the essay the next day.'.

subject: English Language
text: Amina smiled and declined the compliment, saying, 'I just did what was needed.' What is the most likely tone?
explanation: Declining a compliment while attributing success to duty suggests modesty; this fits 'modest' rather than arrogance, hostility, or bewilderment.

subject: English Language
text: The majority of the committee ____ in favour of the proposal.
explanation: When 'majority of' refers to members, verb agrees with plural sense; use plural 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By noon she ______ the report and sent it to her supervisor.
explanation: Past perfect ('had finished') describes an action completed before another past time (by noon).

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'tedious'?
explanation: 'Tedious' denotes something dull or boring; semantic match is 'boring', not danger or brevity.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'He washed his hands of the matter,' 'washed his hands of' most nearly means:
explanation: Idiom 'wash one's hands of' means to refuse involvement or responsibility for something.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised sentence for: 'at noon, dr. Olufemi arrived in abeokuta.'
options: At noon, Dr. Olufemi arrived in Abeokuta.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Sentences start with a capital; titles 'Dr.' and proper noun 'Abeokuta' are capitalised; punctuation after 'Dr.' required.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: 'clever', 'control', 'arrange', 'describe'?
explanation: 'Clever' has stress on the first syllable (CLE-ver); the others (con-TROL, a-RRANGE, de-SCRIBE) stress second syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: ship, sheep, slip, sip?
explanation: 'Sheep' has the long /iː/ vowel while 'ship', 'slip', 'sip' have the short /ɪ/ vowel; vowel quality differs.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main speech function of: 'Would you mind closing the gate?'
explanation: This is a polite request form using 'Would you mind...?' to ask someone to perform an action.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'The committee will approve the proposal tomorrow.' Which is correct?
options: The proposal will be approved by the committee tomorrow.
Tomorrow the committee will be approved by the proposal.
The proposal will approve the committee tomorrow.
The proposal is approving the committee tomorrow.
explanation: Active 'will approve' becomes passive 'will be approved' with object promoted to subject and agent in 'by the committee'.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: 'If I ____ earlier, I wouldn't have missed the exam.'
explanation: Third conditional requires past perfect in 'if' clause: 'had woken up' + result clause with 'would have'.

subject: English Language
text: Rasheed hid his car keys in the house but the car would not start. He had left the battery disconnected for months. What is the most reasonable inference?
options: The keys were the wrong ones.
The car's tyres were flat and stopped it from starting.
The battery was dead, preventing the car from starting.
He locked the doors and so the car refused to start.
explanation: Leaving a battery disconnected for months plausibly causes a dead battery; this explains failure to start by cause-and-effect inference.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct article: 'She became ___ editor of the magazine.'
explanation: Before a noun beginning with vowel sound /ɛ/ (editor) use 'an'; rule: 'an' precedes vowel sounds for smooth pronunciation.
